Class HashSet<E>

    public class HashSet<E>
extends AbstractSet<E>
implements Set<E>, Cloneable, Serializable
    this class implementsSetinterface, backed by a hash table (actually isHashMapsupported by the instance). It does not guarantee the iteration order of the collection; In particular, it does not guarantee that the order will remain unchanged over time. this class allowsnullElement.

    This class provides basic operations (constant-time performanceadd ， remove ， containsandsize), assuming the hash function distributes the correct elements among the buckets. The time required to iterate over this collection is proportional toHashSetThe size of the instance (number of elements) plus the backingHashMapProportional to the sum of the "capacities" (number of buckets) of the instances. Therefore, if iteration performance is important, it is very important not to set the initial capacity too high (or the load factor too low).

    Note that this implementation is not synchronized. If multiple threads access a hash set concurrently, and at least one thread modifies the set, thenRequiredSynchronize externally. This is typically accomplished by synchronizing on an object that naturally encapsulates the collection. If such an object does not exist, you should useCollections.synchronizedSetThe method "wraps" theSet 。 This is best done at creation time to prevent accidental unsynchronized access to the collection: 

      Set s = Collections.synchronizedSet(new HashSet(...));

    This type ofiteratorThe iterator returned by the method isfail-fast: If the set is modified at any time after the iterator is created, except through the iterator's ownremoveExcept for the method, the iterator throwsConcurrentModificationException 。 Therefore, in the case of concurrent modification, the iterator fails fast and cleanly, rather than risking arbitrary, non-deterministic behavior at an unspecified time in the future.

    Please note that the fail-fast behavior of iterators cannot be guaranteed, because in general, it is impossible to make any hard guarantees in the presence of unsynchronized concurrent modification. Fail-fast iterators throw on a best-effort basisConcurrentModificationException 。 Therefore, it is incorrect to write programs that depend on this exception to ensure their correctness:The fail-fast behavior of an iterator should be used only to detect bugs.
